claims.text: Greg Short asserts that relocating out of your hometown is the single easiest lever for increasing luck, because it forces you out of a familiar reference group that has capped your perceived ceiling and into new environments where serendipity and higher-caliber peers are more accessible.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
conditions: Person currently lives in their hometown
Hometown social and geographic environment is lower-ambition than the person's goal level
claims.mechanism: Geographic relocation removes the familiar low-ceiling reference group and exposes the person to higher-ambition peers and opportunities, expanding the surface area on which luck can land.

claims.text: Greg Short argues that being the most capable person (the shark) in your immediate social pond — whether defined by friend group, city of residence, or media consumed — actively decreases your luck, because the reference group sets the ceiling on your expectations, behavior, and opportunities.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.mechanism: The highest performer in any reference group calibrates ambition and behavior to that group's ceiling; when the ceiling is low, potential and luck-generating behaviors are suppressed accordingly.

claims.text: Greg Short claims that the media a person passively consumes — including social media doom-scrolling — functions as a reference group (a pond) with the same luck-suppressing effect as living in the wrong city or surrounding yourself with the wrong people; consuming low-quality media is equivalent to choosing low-quality peers.
claims.speaker: Greg Short
claims.speaker_term: the pond that you are swimming in

practices.text: Move out of your hometown to increase your exposure to higher-ambition peers and environments.
Surround yourself with people who keep you out of trouble and who motivate and inspire you.
Audit the media you consume; avoid doom-scrolling low-quality social media content because it constitutes your reference group and suppresses luck.
